Shadows

Four elevation levels, a tooltip shadow, and four focus rings. Elevation says what sits above what; a focus ring says where the keyboard is.

5 elevations4 focus ringsToken-driven

Elevation

Each sample is drawn by its own token — box-shadow: var(--shadow-*).
LevelTokenValueSampleUse for
card--shadow-card0 0 12px 0 · rgba(15,23,43,0.12)Raised — feature cards, product tiles
card-hover--shadow-card-hover0 4px 12px 0 · rgba(15,23,43,0.08)Card hover state
float--shadow-float0 2px 16px 0 · rgba(15,23,43,0.20)Floating — dropdowns, sticky headers, Flyout Menu
modal--shadow-modal0 8px 24px 0 · rgba(15,23,43,0.32)Highest — dialogs, the product and login flyouts
tooltip--shadow-tooltip0 4px 8px 0 · rgba(0,0,0,0.25)Tooltip — Figma’s blur is 8, not 16

Hierarchy

Higher means closer to the reader. Something that opens over a raised surface goes up a level, never sideways.

Focus rings

A 3px ring at 25%, outside the control’s own 2px border — the border carries the contrast, the ring makes it unmissable. Each ring matches the colour of the border it sits beside.
RingTokenColourSampleUse for
blue--shadow-focus-blueiron-blue/500 · 25%Every form field, and the default
magenta--shadow-focus-magentairon-pink/500 · 25%Primary Button
danger--shadow-focus-dangeriron-red/700 · 25%A form field in error
teal--shadow-focus-tealiron-green/500 · 25%Secondary

Guidelines

✓ Do
  • Use one elevation per layer, and step up for anything that opens over it.
  • Show focus with :focus-visible — a ring for keyboard users, nothing for a mouse click.
  • Keep the 2px border with the ring; under .dark the ring alone can fall below 3:1.
✗ Don't
  • Don’t write a new shadow; if none fits, the layer is probably wrong.
  • Don’t use a shadow where a 1px border would separate the two just as well.
  • Don’t remove a focus ring without replacing it — keyboard users lose their place (WCAG 2.4.7).
